strategy.audience: Developers building autonomous on-chain agents and protocol architects designing credit rails for non-human actors.
strategy.problem_statement: Autonomous agents have mature payment rails to spend what they hold in a wallet, but they cannot safely borrow or take leveraged credit positions because autonomous borrowing requires dynamic, verifiable constraint computation to prevent liquidation.
strategy.angle: For an autonomous agent holding credit, solvency cannot rely on human intervention or static limits; health factor math is the core operating constraint that enables an agent to compute position boundaries and execute auto-signed transactions to maintain solvency programmatically.

briefs.problem_statement: Autonomous agents are restricted to spending only what they hold in cash balances, leaving capital idle and single-purpose because credit rails and real-time solvency controls do not exist for autonomous actors.
briefs.angle: Dynamic health factor math allows an agent to compute constraints and execute auto-signed transactions across unified margin accounts, enabling collateral to actively back credit positions rather than sitting trapped as dormant, single-purpose liquidity.
briefs.audience: DeFi protocol architects and autonomous agent developers building credit systems on Stellar Soroban.
briefs.strongest_objection: Relying on an agent to actively calculate health factor constraints to maintain multi-job collateral introduces execution and insolvency risks that safe, fully funded single-purpose reserves completely eliminate.

briefs.problem_statement: Autonomous agents granted borrowing capabilities inevitably face rapid liquidation cascades if they lack automated, real-time mechanisms to monitor and preserve position solvency during adverse market moves.
briefs.angle: Leverage is easy, but surviving unattended is the hard part; agent-held credit requires policy-bounded constraint calculations and auto-signed corrective transactions that structurally defend health factors before liquidation can occur.
briefs.audience: DeFi developers and autonomous agent builders seeking to integrate automated credit without introducing catastrophic liquidation risk.
briefs.strongest_objection: Because Vanna operates solely on Stellar Soroban testnet without an audit, mainnet track record, or real TVL, policy-bounded auto-signed transactions have not yet been stress-tested against live market volatility to prove liquidation prevention works in practice.

briefs.strongest_objection: Dynamic health factor math and automated rebalancing address execution risk, but they do not solve the foundational counterparty and default underwriting problems required to issue uncollateralized credit to an autonomous program.

ruling.reason: agentic_credit directly aligns with the prompt topic, drawing directly on EV-891de4c980f7 (mature payment rails vs. absent borrowing rails) and EV-d377b1e786dd (agent computes constraints to maintain health factor via auto-signed transactions). Its objection is intellectually honest, noting that health factor math protects solvency and execution, but does not solve uncollateralized underwriting. In contrast, risk_relief grafts a retail/human premise ('keeps them solvent while they sleep') onto agents, and capital_efficiency leans on unsupported concepts of dormant single-purpose reserves.

rankings.note: Strictly adheres to documented facts: agents can pay but lack borrowing rails, and the demo architecture proves health factor math via constraint computation and auto-signed transactions.
Solid grounding on testnet constraints, but imports risk-relief positioning ('keeps them solvent while they sleep') which was drafted for human leverage positions rather than autonomous credit.
Focuses heavily on idle cash balances and multi-job collateral efficiency, which are narrative extrapolations not explicitly backed in the provided evidence.
